changelog.change: Rewritten from the Critical Vector STEMI Equivalents guide — all 8 OMI patterns (De Winter, Wellens A/B, posterior, Smith-modified Sgarbossa, aVR/LMCA, hyperacute T, tombstone/shark-fin, RV MI) with actions. Kept Brugada / hyperK / WPW / TdP / digoxin. Cleared the licensing flag (CV original content).
Initial entry — diagnostic criteria as text.

summary: The occlusion-MI (OMI) paradigm: only ~60% of true coronary occlusions meet classic STEMI criteria. These 8 patterns identify the rest — fully occluded arteries with little or no ST elevation on the standard 12-lead. Plus other high-yield ECGs.

body.text: Missing an OMI pattern is missing the cath window. When the pattern fits and the history fits, activate the cath lab — do not order a stress test and do not 'trend' serial troponins into an occlusion.

rows: Upsloping ST depression ≥ 1 mm at the J-point in V1-V6 + tall, symmetric, peaked T waves. Static — never evolves to classic STE.
Biphasic T waves in V2-V3, in a PAIN-FREE window. ~25%.
Deep symmetric T-wave inversion V2-V3, ST < 1 mm, no Q waves, pain-free. ~75%. Pseudo-normalisation with returning pain = re-occlusion.
Horizontal ST depression ≥ 1 mm V1-V4 (mirror), tall R wave ≥ 0.04 s and R/S ≥ 1 in V1-V2. Confirm with posterior leads V7-V9 STE ≥ 0.5 mm.
ANY of: concordant STE ≥ 1 mm (5 pts); concordant ST depression ≥ 1 mm V1-V3 (3 pts); ST/S ratio ≤ -0.25 (excessively discordant STE, Smith modification, Sn ~91%).
Any occlusion masked by a wide QRS
STE ≥ 1 mm in aVR (and/or aVR > V1) + diffuse ST depression ≥ 1 mm in ≥ 6 leads (I, II, V4-V6). ST depression maximal in II → LM/LAD; in III → RCA.
Tall, broad, asymmetric T waves disproportionate to the QRS (T amplitude > 50% of the R wave in the same lead). Earliest ECG sign — precedes STE by minutes.
Serial ECG q10 min + cardiology STAT
QRS merges with the ST segment and T wave into a single monophasic arch. Massive infarct; cardiogenic-shock risk.
STE ≥ 1 mm in V4R (get right-sided leads). Inferior STEMI with STE in III > II.
Cath + IV fluids + ZERO nitrates / diuretics (preload-dependent)
Coved ST elevation ≥ 2 mm in V1-V3, followed by a negative T wave, little/no isoelectric separation
Saddleback, J-wave ≥ 2 mm, ST stays ≥ 1 mm above baseline
< 1 mm ST elevation, coved or saddleback

items: Hyperkalemia progression: peaked T waves → PR prolongation / P-wave flattening → QRS widening → sine wave → asystole/VF.
WPW: delta wave + short PR (+ wide QRS). Avoid AV-nodal blockers in pre-excited AF.
Torsades de pointes: polymorphic VT on a prolonged QT — treat with IV magnesium, correct K⁺/Mg²⁺, overdrive pacing / isoproterenol for the bradycardia-dependent form.

Digoxin effect (down-sloping 'scooped' ST, the 'Salvador Dalí moustache') vs. digoxin toxicity (almost any arrhythmia — classically bidirectional VT, PAT with block; worse with hypokalemia/hypomagnesemia).
